golden hamsters (a) use their own phenotype(s), rather than that of their siblings or parents, as the basis for kin–recognizing odours of unfamiliar individuals; (b) do not need postnatal association with relatives for this ability, and (c) can recognize kin through odours that are perceived after birth.
